newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-INSPIRED FIORENTINA BRUSH ASIDE BENFICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INSPIRED FIORENTINA BRUSH ASIDE BENFICA.

text.p: An inspired Fiorentina took a big stride towards the semifinals of the European Cup Winners' Cup by beating Benfica 2-0 on Thursday in the first leg of their quarter-final.

Argentine striker Gabriel Batistuta, recapturing the form that has eluded him recently in the Italian league, scored Fiorentina's second with a spectacular volley in the dying seconds to give his side a vital cushion for the second leg in two weeks.
Batistuta latched on to a cross from the right bPiacentini to fire into the roof of the net, giving Benfica's Belgian goalkeeper Michel Preud'Homme no chance.
Batistuta had earlier played a key role in Fiorentina's first, slipping the ball to fellow striker Francisco Baiano to strike home from the edge of the area seconds before halftime.
"He had a great game," said Fiorentina coach Claudio Ranieri, who added that his team appeared to have rediscovered the consistency they had lost recently in serie A.
The Italians are languishing in 12th place only five points away from the relegation zone.
"We needed a game like this to find our feet again," said Ranieri, although he refused to accept that the second leg in Florence would be a formality.
Benfica had their own chances but they could not argue too much with the result. Only several good saves from Preud'Homme had prevented the visitors putting the tie out of reach.
In a two-minute stretch in the middle of the first period, the veteran Belgian made three stunning saves to deny Fiorentina an opening goal.
It was Benfica who had the first chance of the game when captain Joao Vieira Pinto failed to connect properly with his shot after Moroccan Nader Hassan crossed from the right.
Fiorentina goalkeeper Francesco Toldo was called into action in the 24th minute when he flung himself to his right to block a shot from Benfica midfielder Bruno Caires.
Benfica trainer Manuel Jose brought on Romanian Nica Panduru to give greater speed to the midfield for the second half but the Fiorentina defence held firm.
"We needed a goal. We had a good first 30 minutes but we missed three good chances," said Jose.
"Fiorentina's counter-attacks always unsettled us but they were fortunate to score at such a crucial moment at the end of the first half," he said.
Benfica's best chance in the second half fell to Hassan who fired over from close range after a strong run down the right by Vieira Pinto.
"It is going to be difficult in the second leg but you have always got to believe that a win is possible," Jose said.
